Working document — for discussion, not a published result. An internal selection aid for the Energy Suite heat-pump tool: temporary, not linked from the site, and to be removed once the tier cells are chosen. Nothing here is a recommendation about any product.

Heat-pump tier selection — COP @ 5 °F vs capacity maintenance

Every AHRI-certified unit that appears in the ERS retrofit data, positioned by cold-climate efficiency and capacity retention, sized by how often it was actually installed. Use it to place 3 performance tiers × 3–4 nominal capacities by eye — replacing the 36-cell candidate table.

Bubble area ∝ ERS appearances. Dashed-outline bubbles sit outside the plot window and are clamped to the edge, not dropped. Hover any bubble for its identity. ★ marks the 9 units picked for the tier-cell curves and spec table below.

Gate: 7,314 of 15,148 units plotted, covering 298,209 of 439,975 ERS appearances (67.8%). Dropped: units missing any of the three plotted metrics — capacity maintenance (cm): 7,390 · COP @ 5 F (cop): 7,551 · rated capacity @47 F (c47): 3,600. Nothing is imputed.

Tier-cell heating curves (2026-07-29)

The 9 units picked off the scatter above, digitized from their own manufacturer datasheets where one could be found. Solid = interpolated between two published points. Dashed = extrapolated beyond the published range (linear for capacity, floored at published-COP−0.3 for COP, down to the unit's lockout temperature; held flat above the warmest published point, purely so every line stays visible on a shared axis). Spec-sheet table -- calculated vs. AHRI-certified vs. NEEP (-30°C to 20°C)

One row per whole-degree C. Calculated is this page's own digitized curve -- shaded cells are temperatures where a real datasheet point (not interpolation/extrapolation) rounds to that degree. AHRI is hp_units_joined.csv's two certified anchors (COP+capacity at max compressor speed, 5°F; rated capacity, 47°F -- that source carries no Min/Rated/Max split). NEEP republishes AHRI's own Min/Rated/Max Heating table at 47°F/17°F/5°F and one colder extreme -- richer, and it's the same certificate, not a third-party estimate. Blank cells are not zero -- no source publishes a value there. Cooper & Hunter (low <18k) has no NEEP listing.
